content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.10), especially in the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative (especially if > -0.30), particularly in the last 5–7 days of the forecast.
- Avoid sharp upward revisions in the early forecast window if recent sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0 unit; if below -1.5σ, increase by 0.5–1.0 unit.
- Lag correction: if true outcome is > 2σ above forecast at day 1–3, adjust next 3–5 days downward by 0.3–0.7 units.
- Overshoot correction: if forecast peaks > 1.2x recent 10-day high, reduce peak by 0.2–0.5 units and flatten slope.
- Sentiment-weighted bias: if sentiment > 0.15, forecast should be 5–10% higher than baseline; if sentiment < -0.15, reduce by 5–10%.
